Preview, prediction, and how to watch, stream for free. Denis Bouanga of Los Angeles FC looks on during a match against the Portland Timbers at Providence Park on April 13, 2024, in Portland, Oregon. (Image Credit: Frenchieinportland) Cruz Azul hosts LAFC tonight in the second leg of their Concacaf Champions Cup quarterfinal at Estadio Cuauhtémoc, with LAFC holding a commanding aggregate lead. LAFC enters the match in full control of the tie after a dominant 3–0 win over Cruz Azul in the first leg, powered by goals from Son Heung-Min and a David Martínez brace. The performance highlighted LAFC’s clinical edge, converting three goals from just eight total shots and five on target, while absorbing pressure for long stretches. Despite holding only 34.6% possession and being outshot 15–8, LAFC relied on disciplined defending and strong goalkeeping — recording five saves — to maintain the clean sheet and create a decisive advantage in the tie. Cruz Azul, meanwhile, faces a difficult task after being outplayed in Los Angeles, suffering one of its heaviest defeats in recent continental competition. The Liga MX side will now rely on home support and a more aggressive attacking approach to attempt a comeback, needing at least three goals to force extra time. Prediction With a three-goal aggregate advantage and strong attacking form, LAFC is poised to manage the match and advance, even in a challenging road environment. Predicted score: Cruz Azul 2, LAFC 1 (LAFC advance 4–2 on aggregate) Starting Lineups Cruz Azul (3-4-2-1) GK: K. Mier DEF: W. Ditta, É. Lira, G. Piovi MID: O. Campos, A. Palavecino, J. Márquez, C. Rotondi AM: A. Montaño FW: G. Fernández LAFC (4-2-3-1) GK: H. Lloris DEF: E. Segura, N. Tafari, R. Porteous, S. Palencia MID: M. Delgado, M. Choinière AM: D. Bouanga, T. Tillman, D. Martínez FW: S. Heung-Min How to Watch Cruz Azul vs. LAFC The second leg between Cruz Azul and LAFC is set to kick off at 9:00 PM Eastern at Estadio Cuauhtémoc in Puebla, Mexico. The game airs live nationally on FS1 and streams on the FOX One and FOX Sports apps and websites. If you’re a cordcutter without a livestreaming subscription, you can watch the game broadcast for free by signing up for a one-week trial of FOX One on Amazon here. Here's the game preview, prediction, and how to watch, stream for free. Nathan MacKinnon in action for the Avalanche against the New York Islanders on January 6, 2020. (Image Credit: Quintin Soloviev) The Calgary Flames host the Colorado Avalanche tonight at Scotiabank Saddledome in Calgary, Alberta. Colorado enters this matchup at 53–16–11 (117 points), having already secured the Presidents’ Trophy and the top overall seed in the NHL. They’re coming off a 2–1 shootout win over the Edmonton Oilers on Monday, extending their strong late-season form and pushing their current point streak to four games. Their defensive structure has been especially sharp lately, allowing just 1.5 goals per game over their recent stretch, while continuing to generate offense through elite depth and transition play. Calgary, meanwhile, sits at 33–38–9 (75 points) and has been eliminated from playoff contention. The Flames are coming off a 4–1 win over the Utah Mammoth, snapping a three-game skid and showing some late-season fight. Still, their overall profile reflects a rebuilding team — averaging just 2.55 goals per game while allowing 3.15, with defensive inconsistency a recurring issue. The season series has been one-sided. Colorado has already taken the first two meetings — a 9–1 blowout and a 3–1 win — showcasing the gap in depth, pace, and execution between the teams. In those matchups, the Avalanche controlled possession, generated higher shot volume, and capitalized on turnovers, while Calgary struggled to sustain offense. Tonight’s dynamic, however, is different. Colorado is playing the second leg of a back-to-back and may rest key players, while Calgary is at home with nothing to lose. The Flames’ path to competitiveness lies in slowing the pace, limiting Colorado’s transition game, and capitalizing on any fatigue or lineup rotation from the Avalanche. Prediction Expect a competitive game early, especially with Colorado potentially managing minutes on a back-to-back. But the Avalanche’s depth, structure, and ability to generate offense from multiple lines should still carry them. Projected Final Score: Avalanche 4, Flames 2 How to Watch Avalanche vs. Flames Puck drop for tonight’s game between the Avalanche and Flames is set for 9:00 PM Eastern / 7:00 PM Mountain at Scotiabank Saddledome in Calgary. The game airs live locally on Altitude Sports, KTVD My20, and KUSA 9News. Out-of-market viewers can watch the game on NHL Center Ice through their cable or satellite provider. This game — like most out-of-market NHL matchups — also streams live on ESPN+. If you’re an out-of-market viewer looking to watch the game for free on ESPN+, sign up for a free trial from DIRECTV STREAM, Hulu + Live TV, Fubo TV, or YouTube TV. Hulu + Live TV includes Disney+ and ESPN Unlimited as part of its standard plan, along with a host of other major sports channels. Colorado Avalanche vs. Calgary Flames Date: Tuesday, April 14, 2026 Time: 9:00 PM Eastern / 7:00 PM Mountain Venue: Scotiabank Saddledome, Calgary, AB TV: Altitude Sports, KTVD My20, KUSA 9News Streaming: ESPN+ More from Globely News Rockies vs. Astros: Prediction, Lineups, How to Watch (4/14/26)The Colorado Rockies visit the Houston Astros today at Daikin Park. Here’s the prediction, game preview, starting lineups, and how to watch, stream for free. José Altuve has played for the Houston Astros since 2011, earning MVP honors, eight All-Star selections, and leading them to two World Series championships. (Image Credit: Jeffrey Hayes) The Colorado Rockies (6–10) and the Houston Astros (6–11) kick off a three-game set tonight at Daikin Park, as both teams look to stop extended losing streaks in their second series this month. The Rockies have dropped four straight, getting swept by the San Diego Padres just after completing a three-game sweep of the Astros. Against San Diego, Colorado struggled on both sides of the ball in that series, getting outscored 28–12 across four games, continuing a trend of pitching issues and late-game breakdowns. Despite the recent skid, the Rockies showed promise earlier in the season, holding the Astros to just one run in each of their last two games, capping the series with a 9–1 win in the finale. The Astros, meanwhile, return home after a disastrous road trip, having lost eight straight games and going 1–9 over their last 10. Pitching has been the biggest issue, with Houston allowing eight runs per game over their last eight games, and struggling to control games late. They enter with the worst team ERA in the majors (6.50). Offensively, the Astros still have firepower — Yordan Alvarez, José Altuve, and Carlos Correa have all produced. Houston is second in the majors in runs scored (97) and in the top five in batting average and homers. But their losing record despite their success on the plate shows just how bad their pitching has been. The pitching matchup features Michael Lorenzen for Colorado against Colton Gordon for Houston. Lorenzen has struggled early, entering with an 8.36 ERA, though he’s settled down in his last two appearances. That includes a 5.2 innings start against Houston last week in which he gave up just one run. Gordon makes his season debut. He went 6–4 in 2025 with a 5.34 ERA. Prediction With Houston back at home and due for a bounce-back performance, the Astros have the edge despite recent struggles. Final Score Prediction: Houston Astros 6, Colorado Rockies 4 Starting Lineups Colorado Rockies Tyler Freeman — DH Brenton Doyle — CF Hunter Goodman — C Willi Castro — 2B T.J. Rumfield — 1B Ezequiel Tovar — SS Jordan Beck — RF Kyle Karros — 3B Jake McCarthy — LF Starting Pitcher: Michael Lorenzen (RHP) — 1-1, 8.36 ERA, 10K Houston Astros Jose Altuve — 2B Yordan Alvarez — DH Isaac Paredes — 3B Carlos Correa — SS Christian Walker — 1B Cam Smith — RF Joey Loperfido — CF Christian Vázquez — C Brice Matthews — LF Starting Pitcher: Colton Gordon (LHP) — 0-0, — ERA, 0K How to Watch Rockies vs. Astros First pitch is scheduled for 8:10 PM Eastern at Daikin Park in Houston.
